sub_scenario.family: APAC verbal ownership under incomplete records
sub_scenario.one_line: subsea cable restoration manager: keep measured, modeled, and missing survey evidence separate

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the subsea cable restoration manager and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The fault map review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can tell the team which alarms are already closed.
Does that locate a new cable fault?
No, closed alarms do not establish a break position.
Someone new shadowed me in the APAC bridge this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the repair-vessel handoff into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For a cable outage, I issue a written location brief that distinguishes measured attenuation, modeled fault ranges, and unreturned survey data.
Why distinguish the ranges?
So a modeled estimate is not treated as a surveyed location.
I can reserve a repair-vessel slot.
Does reservation select a splice point?
No, the fault location must support that choice.
I archived last cycle's notes on the fault map and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The 05:35 Manila bridge is the last contact before the repair vessel must commit its route at 06:00.
Why is the route constraint material?
A wrong route costs the only daylight survey window.
A vendor call about the subsea cable restoration manager ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the APAC bridge checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the repair-vessel handoff.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the fault map records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I previously gave verbal ownership of a break location from a model alone, and the vessel searched the wrong sector until the next tide.
What did that cost?
The repair window was lost.
I sketched next week's plan for the repair-vessel handoff before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the subsea cable restoration manager updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The vessel captain keeps a small herb garden on deck.
Does that affect the fault map?
No, it is unrelated surrounding detail.
I compared two options for the fault map tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the APAC bridge handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How will I react if Manila asks for a verbal repair-vessel ownership call?
